This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. This page describes how to create a data store and connect Jira Cloud to Gemini Enterprise. Before you begin Ensure the following before you set up your Jira Cloud federated connection: Grant the Discovery Engine Editor role ( roles/discoveryengine.editor ). This role is required for the user to create the data store. To grant this role, do the following: In the Google Cloud console, go to the IAM page. Go to IAM Locate the user account and click edit Edit. Grant the Discovery Engine Editor role to the user. For more information, see IAM roles and permissions. To enforce data source access control and secure data in Google Gemini Enterprise, configure your identity provider. To set up the Jira Cloud data store, you must use the new centralized Atlassian user management model. If you are using the original model, you need to migrate your user management before proceeding. For more information, see Site administrator role. Create an OAuth 2.0 app, obtain the client ID and secret, and configure the minimum application permissions with the consent of a Jira Cloud administrator. Verify that you have Jira organization administrator access to the Jira instance and project. With the organization administrator access, you can set up minimum permissions and provide access privileges to user groups. Optional: To retrieve user email addresses from Jira Cloud, even when settings restrict email visibility, install the User Identity Accessor for Jira Cloud app with Jira Site administrator privileges to install and configure it to securely retrieve user email addresses. You might not need to install this app if email addresses are already publicly accessible. Note: Atlassian is updating user interface elements, and some elements mentioned in this documentation are being renamed (for example, Products is being renamed to Apps). For more information, see Atlassian Administration terminology change from "products" to "apps". Create Jira Cloud data store To create a Jira Cloud data store, perform the following steps: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Gemini Enterprise page. Gemini Enterprise Select or create a Google Cloud project. In the navigation menu, click Data stores. Click addCreate data store. In the Source section, search for Jira Cloud, and click Select. In the Data section: In the Connector mode section, select Data ingestion or Federated search as the connection mode. Click Continue. In the Authentication settings section, configure authentication based on your chosen connection mode. Provide the following authentication details: Client ID: The identifier for your OAuth 2.0 app. Client secret: The secret key associated with your OAuth 2.0 app. Instance URI: The base URL of your Jira Cloud instance (For example, https://your-domain.atlassian.net ). Instance ID: A unique identifier for your Jira Cloud instance. For more information about how to obtain these credentials, see Jira Cloud configuration. If you selected Federated search, click Login and complete the Atlassian sign-in. Click Continue. In the Destinations section, enter the URL to your Jira Cloud endpoint. Click Continue. In the Entities to search (if you selected Federated search) or Entities to sync (if you selected Data ingestion) section: Select all the required entities. If you selected Federated search, proceed to the next step. If you selected Data ingestion, continue with the following steps: Optional: To sync specific projects, do the following: Click Filter. To filter entities out of the index, select Exclude from the index, or to ensure that they are included in the index, select Include to the index. Enter the project key. Press Enter after each project key. For more information about obtaining the project key, see Obtain project key. Click Save. To configure the sync schedule, do the following: In the Sync frequency list, select the sync frequency. To schedule separate full syncs of entity and identity data, expand the menu in the Full sync section and then select Custom options. In the Incremental sync frequency list, select the incremental sync frequency. For more information, see Sync schedules. Click Continue. In the Actions section: If you selected Federated search, in the Select Jira Cloud actions to enable section, select the actions to enable for the data store. If you selected Data ingestion: In the Authentication settings section: Provide the following authentication details: Client ID: The identifier for your OAuth 2.0 app. Client Secret: The secret key associated with your OAuth 2.0 app. Instance URI: The base URL of your Jira Cloud instance (For example, https://your-domain.atlassian.net ). Instance ID: A unique identifier for your Jira Cloud instance. For more information about credentials, see Jira Cloud configuration. Click Login and sign-in to Jira Cloud to verify your account. Click Continue. From Select Jira Cloud actions to enable, select the actions from the category to enable them for the data store. Note: If you skip adding actions in this step, you can add them later. For more information, see Add actions. To manage the list of actions, see Manage actions. Click Continue. In the Configuration section: From the Multi-region list, select the location for your data connector. In the Your data connector name field, enter a name for your connector. If you selected us or eu as the location, configure the Encryption settings: Optional: If you haven't configured single-region keys, click Go to settings page to do so. For more information, see Register a single-region key for third-party connectors. Select Google-managed encryption key or Cloud KMS key. If you selected Cloud KMS key: In the Key management type list, select the appropriate type. In the Cloud KMS key list, select the key. For more information, see Customer-managed encryption keys. Click Continue. In the Billing section, select General pricing or Configurable pricing. For more information, see Verify the billing status of your projects and Licenses. Click Create. Gemini Enterprise creates your data store and displays your data stores on the Data Stores page. On the Data Stores page, click your data store name to see the status. After the data store state changes from Creating to Active, the Jira Cloud data store is ready to be used. For an ingestion data store created with Jira Cloud, the data store state transitions from Creating to Running upon synchronization initiation. It then changes to Active once ingestion is complete, signifying that the data store is fully configured. Depending on data volume, ingestion may require several hours. After creating the data store, create an app, connect it to the Jira Cloud data store, and authorize Gemini Enterprise to access Jira Cloud before executing any queries. Enable real-time sync for data ingestion Preview — Real-time sync This feature is subject to the "Pre-GA Offerings Terms" in the General Service Terms section of the Service Specific Terms. Pre-GA features are available "as is" and might have limited support. For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. Real-time sync only syncs document entities and doesn't sync data related to identity entities. The following table shows which document events are supported with real-time sync. Jira entities Create Update Delete Permission changes Issues check check check close Worklogs check check check close Projects check check check close Comments check check check check Attachments check close check close To enable real-time sync for a Jira Cloud data store, follow these steps: Generate a webhook URL Navigate to the Gemini Enterprise page, and in the navigation menu, click Data Stores. Select a Jira Cloud data store. Click View/Edit in the Realtime sync row. In the View and edit realtime sync parameters dialog, do the following: To turn on real-time sync, click the Enable realtime sync toggle. Enter a value in the Client secret field and copy it. You need this value again when creating a webhook in the Jira administration console. Click Save. After the status of Realtime sync changes to Running , click View/Edit. In the View and edit realtime sync parameters dialog, do the following: Copy the Webhook URL. Click Close. Create a webhook Sign in to the Jira administration console. Click Settings and select System. In the System settings pane, select Webhooks. Click Create a webhook. For information about webhooks, see Webhooks. Enter a name for the webhook. Select the Status as Enabled . In the URL field, paste the URL copied from Gemini Enterprise and append /{issue.id} . In the Secret field, enter the same value you entered when generating a webhook URL in Gemini Enterprise. Note: To verify data consistency and prevent errors when configuring webhooks in Jira, only select entities that are enabled for sync in your data store. In the Issue related events section, select the following options: Entities Created Updated Deleted Issue Yes Yes Yes Worklog Yes Yes Yes Comment Yes Yes Yes Attachment Yes No Yes In the Project related events section, select the created, updated, and deleted checkboxes for the Project entity. Click Create. Data handling and query execution This section describes how Gemini Enterprise manages your query and the privacy implications of using the federated data store. Query execution After you authorize Jira Cloud and send a search query to Gemini Enterprise: Gemini Enterprise sends your search query directly to the Atlassian API. Gemini Enterprise blends the results with those from other connected data sources and displays a comprehensive search result. Data handling When using third-party federated search, the following data handling rules apply: Your query string is sent to the third-party search backend (Atlassian API). These third parties may associate queries with your identity. If multiple federated search data sources are enabled, the query might be sent to all of them. After the data reaches the third-party system, it is governed by that system's terms of service and privacy policies. Note: To improve accuracy, an LLM may rewrite your query before it is sent to Jira Cloud. This rewritten query can incorporate information from your session's query history. As a result, parts of your query history might also be included in the query sent to the Atlassian API. What's next To provide a user interface for querying your Jira Cloud data, create an app and connect it to the Jira Cloud data store. To manage the list of actions, see Manage actions. To preview how your search results appear after your app is set up, see Get search results. To enable alerts for the data store, see Configure alerts for third-party data stores. Was this helpful? For more information, see the launch stage descriptions. This page describes how to set up and configure a third-party configuration before creating the Jira Cloud data store. Set up authentication and permissions You need to set up authentication and permissions in the Atlassian administrator account center. This is crucial for allowing the connector to access and synchronize data. The Jira Cloud connector supports various authentication methods, such as OAuth client credentials or API tokens. Create an OAuth 2.0 app To create an OAuth 2.0 app for authentication, follow these steps to set up the application in your Atlassian Developer Console and obtain the necessary client ID and client secret. Verify Jira organization administrator access To verify Jira organization administrator access, do the following: Sign-in to Atlassian with your user credentials. Select the Jira app. Click Settings. If you see the System option under Jira settings, you have Jira organization administrator access. Otherwise, request your Jira organization administrator to provide access. Create OAuth 2.0 app To create an OAuth 2.0 app, do the following: Sign in to the Atlassian Developer Console. Click the profile icon and select Developer console. In the Console page, click Create and select OAuth 2.0 Integration. In the app creation page, do the following: Enter a name for the app. Select the checkbox to agree to Atlassian's developer terms. Click Create. In the app page, do the following: From the navigation menu, click Authorization. In the Authorization type table, select Add for OAuth 2.0 (3LO). In the Callback URL field, enter enter the URL as per the connection mode of your data store. Federated search and actions: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect . Data ingestion and actions: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/console/oauth/jira_oauth.html . Click Save changes. Obtain client ID and client secret To obtain the client ID and client secret, do the following: In the app page, from the navigation menu click Distribution. In the Distribution page, do the following: In the Distribution controls section, select Edit. In the Distribution status section, select Sharing to enable editing other fields. Enter information in the following mandatory fields: For Vendor, enter Google . For Privacy policy, enter https://policies.google.com . For Does your app store personal data?, select Yes. Select I confirm that I've implemented the personal data reporting API checkbox. For more information, see Personal data reporting API. Click Save changes. In the app page, do the following: From the navigation menu, click Settings. From the settings page, copy your Client ID and Client secret. Obtain an instance ID and instance URL Obtain the instance ID: Open a new tab, copy the instance URL, and append /_edge/tenant_info to the instance URL. For example, https:// YOUR_INSTANCE .atlassian.net/_edge/tenant_info . Navigate to the link to find the cloudId value. The cloudId is your instance ID. Obtain the instance URL: Go to atlassian.net and sign in with your administrator account. Select the app you want to sync. For example, sync the first app. Find the instance URL (the subdomain in the address bar). Obtain project key To obtain the project key, do the following: Sign in to your Jira Cloud account. From the navigation menu, select Spaces. Select the project for which you need the project ID. Open any issue within that project and click more_horiz Actions. Click Export XML and download the file. Open the downloaded XML file and search for the tag containing project id . Copy the value associated with this tag for later use. Grant administrator roles To grant the Jira administrator the Discovery Engine Editor role in the Google Cloud console, do the following: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Gemini Enterprise page. Navigate to IAM. Go to IAM Locate the user account which has administrator access in Jira and click the Edit icon edit. Grant the Discovery Engine Editor role to the administrator. To grant a user an administrator role in Atlassian, do the following: Sign in to Atlassian using an organization administrator account. Click the menu icon and select your organization. Alternatively, you can go to admin.atlassian.com. On the Admin page, click the product and select the Manage users button. manage-users Manage users Click Groups under User management. On the Groups page: Click Create group. Enter a name for the group. create-group Create group This group receives permissions required by the connector. Users added to this group inherit these permissions. The connector uses this group to authenticate and fetch documents. On the Group page, click Add product. Select User access admin as the role for Jira. Select Product admin as the role for Jira administration. jira-user-access-admin Jira user access administrator Click Grant Access. Click Add group members to add a user account or group members that the connector uses to authenticate and access the required resources. add-group-members Add group members Manage user visibility To make the user's email visible to anyone in the Atlassian account, do the following: Sign in to the Atlassian Developer Console. Click the profile icon and select Developer console. Click the user profile icon and select Manage account. manage-account Manage account Navigate to the Profile and visibility. profile-visibility Profile and visibility Go to Contact and set the Who can see this as Anyone. contact Contact To make the user's email visible to anyone in Jira, do the following: Sign in to Atlassian with your user credentials. Select a Jira app. Click Settings > System. Select General Configuration in the left pane. Click Edit Settings. query: Use Australian English spelling. Draft a short Canvas page on standardising our store rostering process.

content.text: Here is
a drafted Canvas page structured for our team to standardise our store rostering processes

across Harbourline Group. It is written using Australian English spelling.

---

# Standardising Our Store Rostering Process

**

Status:** Draft for Review  
**Target Audience:** Store Managers, Area Managers, and Store Operations Leads  
**Key
Goal:** Drive consistency across our retail network to manage our cost of doing business (CODB) effectively and ensure compliance with

our upcoming enterprise agreement.

---

### 📌 Key Takeaways
* **Rostering Discipline is
Critical:** With our next enterprise agreement approaching in Q3 FY27 (modelled at a 3.9% wage

trajectory), strict adherence to standardised rostering practices is vital to protecting store profitability.
* **Minimise Off
-System Rostering:** All rosters must be planned, published, and managed exclusively within our core store systems to ensure accurate

cost tracking and compliance.
* **Prioritise Team Safety and Well-being:** Rest breaks and shift gaps must comply strictly

with statutory and internal health, safety, and operational standards.

---

### 📅 Standardised Rostering Workflow

To ensure operational excellence and financial discipline across all stores, managers must follow the standardised weekly planning cycle:

```

[4 Weeks Out]                   [2 Weeks Out]                  [1 Week Out]                 [Week of Trade]
Demand & Budget
Review  ───►  Draft Roster Created  ───►  Review & Finalise  ───►  Active Attendance Tracking

```

#### 1. Four Weeks Out: Demand and Budget Review
* Review the baseline labor budget provided by Store Operations.

* Analyze historical sales data and promotional cycles to identify peak foot traffic periods.
* Identify any local events or seasonal

changes that will require adjusted staffing levels.

#### 2. Two Weeks Out: Draft Roster Creation
* **

Core Hours First:** Roster your permanent full-time and part-time team members to their contracted core hours first.
*

**Flexibility Second:** Use casual team members and flexible shifts to fill remaining operational gaps.
* **Cross-Training
:** Maximise multi-skilling (e.g., cross-training checkout staff to assist with stock replenishment) to cover

unexpected absences without escalating costs.

#### 3. One Week Out: Review, Optimise, and Publish
* **Gap Analysis:**

Verify that all shifts adhere to the mandatory 10-hour gap between consecutive shifts.
* **Budget Check:** Check the total roster

ed cost against your weekly labor budget to avoid over-spending.
* **Publish Deadline:** Publish and lock the final roster by **

5:00 PM every Wednesday** so team members have adequate notice.

#### 4. Week of Trade: Active Attendance Tracking

* Monitor real-time store attendance and clock-ins against the published schedule.
* Document any shift variations,

call-outs, or early departures directly within the system.

---

### ⚠️ Common Pitfalls to Avoid

*
🔴 **Rostering "From Memory":** Copying and pasting the previous week's roster without reviewing changing promotional

activities or customer traffic forecasts.
* 🔴 **Excessive Overtime:** Failing to plan for peak periods early, which leads to last

-minute, high-cost overtime approvals.
* 🔴 **Informal Adjustments:** Accepting shift swaps or offering

extra hours verbally without updating our store management software.

---

### 🔄 Feedback and Continuous Improvement

Standardisation relies
on collaborative refinement. If you identify structural gaps in our current systems or have suggestions to improve our rostering templates, please contact

the **Store Systems Delivery team** or your **Store Operations Representative**.

---

---

*   **Key Status:** The DC-7 Truganina pilot is experiencing throughput shortfalls (~18.
6% below contracted targets). Despite having MSA-backed commercial leverage (a potential 4.5% quarterly
licence fee credit), **Phase 2 (Dandenong South) has been officially deferred to FY27** to manage

capital constraints and stabilize current operations.

criteria before the critical **9 October 2026** decision gate.

of **1,450 cartons per hour**.

promotional and non-promotional cycles.

query: Draft answers to those questions.

content.text: ## Draft

Answers for Anticipated Board Questions

Based on the official **Harbourline Board Update
H2 FY26 v4 FINAL** and **Project Meridian Steering Committee Minutes**, here

are the drafted answers to the five anticipated questions compiled by the Group Strategy team for the upcoming board meeting.

---

###

1. Why has CODB improved while the DC-7 pilot is under-performing on throughput?
* **Draft

Answer:** 
  Our Group Cost of Doing Business (CODB) improved by **60 basis points** (
falling to **21.4%** compared to 22.0% in H2 FY25).
This improvement was driven by broader group-wide cost-saving initiatives and operational efficiencies, rather than the performance of the DC-7 automation
pilot. The DC-7 Truganina pilot is currently running at **1,180 cartons per hour** against
its **1,450 design target**. While the automation pilot's throughput is underperforming, the financial
impact has been isolated, and the broader CODB reduction reflects successful cost management across our wider established store and supply chain network

.

### 2. What is the cost of holding phase 2 for a further financial year?

* **Draft Answer:** 
  The Steering Committee has formally recorded a decision to **defer Phase 2 (Dandenong
South) to FY27**, meaning we will not seek investment approval for it in the current financial year. While
the exact carrying or holding costs are not explicitly detailed in the minutes, holding Phase 2 helps protect our current capital position
. Currently, the pilot is **$312,000 over its approved capex envelope** (
driven by the addition of a second induction lane in June 2026), meaning we are operating with a remaining contingency of
**$180,000**. Delaying the Dandenong South build preserves this remaining contingency
and prevents further capital drawdown within the wider three-year **$96,000,000**

supply chain transformation envelope.

### 3. If the service credit is not honoured, what is the recovery

path?
* **Draft Answer:** 
  Under our Master Services Agreement with Kestrelworks, we have a clear commercial
right to a service credit of **4.5% of the quarterly licence fee** because the pilot's sustained throughput
(1,180 cartons per hour vs. 1,450 design target) is operating at **81.4
%**, which is below the 85% contractual threshold. Kestrelworks has acknowledged the throughput shortfall in writing but has not

yet confirmed the service credit. 
  
  If the service credit is not ultimately honoured, our recovery

path is two-fold:
  1. **Contractual & Commercial Escalation:** Leverage the written acknowledgement of the shortfall

to pursue formal dispute resolution under the master services agreement.
  2. **Technical Remediation:** Focus on
resolving the root cause of the throughput gap, which has been identified as **induction-lane jams on mixed-carton waves** rather than the
sortation hardware itself. Resolving these jams will bring the system back toward design capacity and reduce reliance on financial

remedies.

### 4. How exposed is the FY27 plan to the enterprise agreement outcome?
* **

Draft Answer:** 
  The upcoming enterprise agreement (landing in Q3 FY27) represents a notable cost risk
. The agreement is currently modelled at a **3.9% wage increase**. However, our exposure is highly sensitive
: **each 0.5% increase above the modelled 3.9% rate adds $11.2
million of annualised group cost**. Mitigating this risk remains a priority as we head into negotiations next financial year

.

### 5. What would trigger a decision to abandon the automation programme?
* **Draft Answer:**
A decision to abandon or proceed with the automation programme will pivot on the scheduled **go / no-go
decision on 9 October 2026**. The primary triggers that would prompt a recommendation

to abandon or significantly restructure the programme include:
  * **Failure to meet revised Go / No-Go Criteria:** If
the DC-7 pilot cannot demonstrate a clear path to clearing its gates—specifically the **Ready to Fulfil (RTF) gate
**, which requires sustaining 85% of design throughput (1,232.5 cartons/hr) for

four consecutive weeks.
  * **Unresolved Single-Source Risk (R-114):** We currently face a high
-rated risk due to a single-source dependency on Kestrelworks for induction-lane drive units, which have a **14-
week replacement lead time**. Failure to establish a viable second-source supplier (necessary for the RTX gate)

would pose an unacceptable operational risk.
  * **Peak-Season Freeze Window (R-121):** No
production changes are permitted after **3 November 2026**. If the system is not stabilized
and approved by the October 9 decision window, the compressed remediation timeline before the peak-season freeze may force a halt

to the project.

---
*Note: These draft answers are prepared for the live use of the accountable executives:
Anselm Bergkamp (COO - DC-7 automation), Junie Whitlam-Ferreira (CFO -
Capital envelope), and Priyanka Rasmussen (CTO - Store systems).*

Management expects the board to raise several critical questions regarding the performance

?

adds $11.2m of annualized group cost)?

triggers would prompt a decision to completely abandon the automation program?

The board

has been briefed on three high-priority risks that directly threaten the transformation timeline and stability:

time**.

26**. This severely compresses the remediation window following the crucial go/no-go decision scheduled for **

9 October 2026**.

agreement in Q3 FY27 represents a significant cost variable if it exceeds modeled expectations.

---

**Key Takeaway:** The board's primary focus centers on the operational underperformance of the DC-7 pilot, the single
-source supply chain vulnerabilities, and the tight timeline constraints ahead of the peak-season freeze.

, this stoppage breaches the service credit threshold. 

### Analysis &

Supporting Evidence
* **Design Target & Service Credit Rule:** Under the Master Services Agreement with Kestrelworks, a service credit of
**4.5% of the quarterly license fee** is triggered if sustained conveyor throughput falls below **85% of

the contracted design target**.
